## Loading the packages you need for this workflow
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
# install.packages("kableExtra")
```

Load a new data set from three class trips to Skidaway Island on the Georgia coast. Fish morphometrics were collected on various species caught by net in the fall season of each year.  
Download Data here:  

```{r}

df_total <- read.csv("~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-MercerUniversity/Merged Synced Documents/Teaching_Documents/BIO_421/2025_Fall/Class_Data_Sets/Fish Trawl Data Total.csv") 


df_total <- df_total %>% 
  rename(name = Taxon) %>%
  mutate(name = str_trim(name)) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.factor(Skidaway_year))
```

## Using the filter() function 

```{r}
df_total %>% 
  filter(name == "Whiting") %>%
  summarize(count = n(), 
            mean = mean(Length_AP) %>% round(2), 
            sd = sd(Length_AP) %>% round(2)) %>% 
  kable(caption = "Summary Statistics for the Whiting Fish") %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Arial")

df_total %>% 
  filter(Length_AP > 100) %>% 
  summarize(count = n(), 
            mean = mean(Length_AP) %>% round(2), 
            sd = sd(Length_AP) %>% round(2)) %>% 
  kable(caption = "Summary Statistics for Fish > 100 cm") %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Arial")
```

## The group_by() %>% summarize() move is key for your wrangling.

```{r}
df_total %>% 
  group_by(name) %>% 
  summarize(count = n(), 
            mean = mean(Length_AP) %>% round(2), 
            sd = sd(Length_AP) %>% round(2)) %>% 
  kable(caption = "Summary Statistics by Fish Type") %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Arial")

# What's the difference between these two code chunks?
df_total %>% 
  group_by(name, Skidaway_year) %>% 
  summarize(count = n(), 
            mean = mean(Length_AP) %>% round(2), 
            sd = sd(Length_AP) %>% round(3)) %>% 
  kable(caption = "Summary Statistics by Fish Type") %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Arial")
```

## Create a new Variable with the mutate() function  

This new variable is the geometric mean of the three length variables describing overall fish size.

```{r}
df_new <- df_total %>% 
  mutate(Geom_mean = (Length_AP*Length_ML*Length_DV)^(1/3)) %>% 
  select(year, name, Length_AP, Length_ML, Length_DV, Geom_mean) 

df_sum <- df_total %>% 
  mutate(Geom_mean = (Length_AP*Length_ML*Length_DV)^(1/3)) %>% 
  select(year, name, Length_AP, Length_ML, Length_DV, Geom_mean) |> 
  group_by(name) %>% 
  summarize(count = n(), 
            mean = mean(Geom_mean) %>% round(2), 
            sd = sd(Geom_mean) %>% round(2))

df_sum %>% 
  kable(caption = "Summary Statistics of Geometric Mean by Fish Type") %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Arial")
```


## Make Some Bar Plots Showing Sample Counts

```{r}
df_new %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = year)) +
    geom_bar(mapping = aes(fill = name), position = "dodge")

df_new %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = year)) +
    geom_bar(mapping = aes(fill = name), position = "fill")

df_new %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = year)) +
    geom_bar(mapping = aes(fill = name), position = "stack")
```



## We can "melt" the data so that all four columns of size data are faceted individually

```{r}
df_melt <- df_new %>% 
  pivot_longer(3:6, names_to = "variable_name", values_to = "measurement")
# What's the "3:6" designation above
# inspect this object and see how it's different.
```

## Now you can plot all four measurements in one graph but on different facets.

```{r}
df_melt %>% 
  # filter(variable_name != "Geom_mean") %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = name, y = measurement)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    labs(title = "3 Dimensions of Size in Fish Trawl Data") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    facet_grid(. ~ variable_name) 

df_melt %>% 
  # filter(variable_name != "Geom_mean") %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = name, y = measurement, fill = year)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(mapping = aes(color = year), width = 0.15) +
    labs(title = "3 Dimensions of Size in Fish Trawl Data") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    facet_grid(. ~ variable_name) 

# How many IVs are there in the graph?
# Copy and paste this code and change your IVs around.

```

## Let's create some scatterplots to see how lengths scale with each other

```{r}
# For this you can go back to the non-melted dataset, df_new.
df_new %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Length_AP, Length_ML)) + 
    geom_point(mapping = aes(color = name))

df_new %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Length_AP, Length_ML)) + 
    geom_point(mapping = aes(color = name)) +
    geom_smooth(method = lm)

df_new %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Length_AP, Length_ML)) + 
    geom_point(mapping = aes(color = name)) + 
    geom_smooth(method = lm) +
    facet_grid(. ~ year)

df_new %>% 
  mutate(log_AP = log10(Length_AP)) %>% 
  mutate(log_ML = log10(Length_ML)) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = log_AP, log_ML)) + 
    geom_point(mapping = aes(color = name)) + 
    geom_smooth(method = lm) +
    facet_grid(. ~ year) +
    labs(title = "3 Years of Length and Width Scaling in Fish Trawl Data")
```
